newsitem.title: INDIA: India Essel plans share buyback-paper.
newsitem.headline: India Essel plans share buyback-paper.

text.p: Essel Packaging, India's leading manufacturer of laminated tubes, plans to buy back its shares at a premium to the current price, the Economic Times newspaper said on Friday.

The share buyback of about 10-20 percent of the company's 150 million rupee equity capital is likely to be done at about 225 rupees per share, the paper quoted Subhash Chandra, chairman of Essel Packaging Chandra, as saying.
The company will buy back shares from the market after the government grants permission to Indian companies, the report said.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Essel shares jumped 9.0 rupees, or 5.6 percent, to a new 52-week high at the Bombay exchange on Friday after the buyback news.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his budget proposals for the 1997/98 (April-March) said that buybacks of shares would be allowed under a new company law for which a legislative bill would be introduced in parliament.
Sales of Essel Packaging rose 27 percent to 325.1 million rupees in the first quarter ending June 30, 1997 against the year-ago period, the paper said.
